question: Which specific model claims can this independent manufacturer reference test?

reference_identity.title: 230-V, 3.5-kW PFC With >98% Efficiency, Optimized for BOM and Size Reference Design
reference_identity.author: Texas Instruments, Incorporated
reference_identity.pages_note: pdfinfo reports 17 pages; the BSD 'file' utility reported 10. Text extraction recovered 17 pages of content; the pdfinfo count is used.
reference_identity.creator: Antenna House XSL Formatter V7.4 R1

populated_circuit.topology: single-phase, non-interleaved, non-bridgeless continuous-conduction-mode (CCM) boost PFC; passive diode-bridge front end
populated_circuit.topology_evidence: Description p.1: 'continuous-conduction-mode (CCM) boost converter'; System Design Theory p.5; no interleaving, bridgeless, or totem-pole language anywhere in the retained document
populated_circuit.gate_driver: UCC27524 (dual low-side; 5 A source / 5 A sink peak ratings; 17 ns typical propagation delay)
populated_circuit.gate_driver_evidence: printed p.5 (Sec 2.2.2); printed p.8 lists 'UCC28180 PFC controller UCC27524 gate driver'
populated_circuit.bias_supply: UCC28881 on-board 15 V bias (700 V, 14 ohm integrated MOSFET)
populated_circuit.parallel_switch_count_evidence: printed p.8 (Sec 2.3.8): 'Diode bridge BR1, MOSFET Q1, Q6, power diode D1, D3 are mounted on heatsink'. Two MOSFET designators on one shared heatsink in a single-boost topology, with a dual-channel driver documented as able to drive 'two switches in parallel with a single input signal' (printed p.5). Parallelism is strongly implied but never stated verbatim; the series/parallel connection and the per-device current-sharing ratio must come from the schematic/BOM, which is NOT contained in the retained PDF (Sec 4.1: 'Download all schematics at TIDA-00779').
populated_circuit.boost_diode_type: not stated in the retained document (power diode type and count of parallel die unresolved)
populated_circuit.gate_network: 22 ohm series gate resistor with an antiparallel 100 V / 1 A Schottky (or switching) diode for fast turn-off, plus 10 kohm gate-to-ground; gate drive clamped at 15.2 V internally
populated_circuit.boost_inductor_evidence: printed p.6 (Sec 2.3.3): calculated Lmin 174 uH, 'actual value ... used is LMIN = 180 uH'
populated_circuit.output_capacitance_evidence: printed p.6 (Sec 2.3.2): 2286 uF calculated, 2040 uF selected
populated_circuit.output_voltage_mode: boost follower: DC bus varies with peak line voltage (see Table 3-3)

model_case_under_test.gate_bias_v: 12 V nominal (contract baseline_drive_v); retained no-assist report scenario uses 12.6 V
model_case_under_test.external_gate_r_ohm: 4.7 (contract); reported scenarios vary 10.0 / 15.0 / 18.5 by driver profile

claimed_overlap_term_w.statement: approximately 37 W switching-overlap loss on the boost switch
claimed_overlap_term_w.contract_note: partial switch/gate loss only; not a measurement and not whole-assembly. The overlap term is a component of this subtotal, not the subtotal itself.

gate_bias_v.note: 15 V bias rail / 15.2 V clamp; not a measured gate-pin high level

efficiency_table_230v.caption: Table 3-1. Performance Data Under 230-V AC Input

rows.exclusion_reason: P=VI*PF identity not satisfied: 229.80*1.2858*0.9340=276.0 W vs printed 238.4 W (light-load, THD 22.9%); excluded
P=VI*PF: 229.31*3.1522*1.0=722.8 W vs printed 708.6 W (2.0% mismatch); excluded
P=VI*PF: 227.62*11.366*1.0=2587.1 W vs printed 2349.7 W (10.1% mismatch); excluded
POUT (2560.7 W) > PIN (2513.6 W) while printed efficiency is 97.974%; PIN*eff=2462.7 W; excluded (this is the row flagged in benchmark/REPORT.md)

rows.exclusion_reason: POUT field printed 2.0102 W; VOUT*IOUT=2010.2 W and PIN*eff=2010.2 W; decimal-field defect; excluded
PIN field printed 2.1985 W; VIN*IIN*PF=2198.0 W; POUT>PIN; decimal-field defect; excluded
POUT field printed equal to PINAC (2687.4 W); VOUT*IOUT=2640.9 W and PIN*eff=2640.9 W; excluded

line_to_bus_map.caption: Table 3-3. Standby Power and Output Voltage (also the boost-follower line-to-bus map)

device_temperatures.conditions: room temperature 25 C, closed enclosure, no airflow, full load, 30 minutes before capture; heatsink cooled by two 27 CFM / 24 VDC / 2.64 W fans, one on each side
device_temperatures.note: No per-device bias current or junction temperature is published as a number; MOSFET/IGBT die temperatures must not be inferred from a thermal image label.

waveform_observability.whole_board_efficiency_is_not_event_ener: EXPLICIT: Table 3-1/3-2 Pin and Pout are whole-board, whole-line-cycle input/output powers from a power analyzer. They are NOT a per-device turn-on/turn-off energy (Eon/Eoff) measurement and cannot be treated as one.
why_event_energy_cannot_be_extracted: Figures 3-6/3-7 show gate voltage and drain-to-source voltage but CH4 is AC input current, not the boost switch drain current; no current probe on the switch transition is published.
No numeric time base, amplitude values, or vertical/horizontal scale values are present in the document text layer for Figures 3-6/3-7; only the image exists.
The line phase and load at which Figures 3-6/3-7 were captured are not stated, so no event current is associated with them.
No commutation/diode-recovery energy, no loop-inductance value, and no ringing data are published.
No de-embedding or probe-bandwidth statement accompanies the switching figures.
waveform_observability.conclusion: The reference supports a whole-board efficiency/topology comparison only. It does not expose any per-event switching energy, event current, gate-current waveform, or per-device loss.

applicability_table.source_row: Table 3-1/3-2 VOUT column; Table 3-3 line->VOUT; Figures 3-2/3-3
applicability_table.source_conditions: steady-state DC bus, boost-follower (bus tracks line)
applicability_table.reason: Bus follows line: 400 V is reached only near 270 V line. There is no TI row with a low line (120 V) and a 400 V bus. The model case (120 V line, 400 V bus) does not exist in the reference.

applicability_table.source_row: Sec 2.3.1 'This design uses a 45kHz switching frequency'; Table 1-1
applicability_table.source_value: 45000 Hz (44000 Hz with the 47 kohm FREQ resistor actually fitted)
applicability_table.reason: 45 kHz design / 44 kHz actual vs 129.107 kHz model case: 2.87x frequency mismatch; overlap loss scales with frequency.

The reference publishes only AC input RMS current and output DC current. No boost-switch instantaneous turn-on drain current is published; Figures 3-6/3-7 carry no drain-current channel and no numeric values.
Same as turn_on_current_a: no instantaneous switch drain current is published.

Duty-weighted per-switch RMS is not published. IINAC is line-frequency input RMS and is not the switch RMS (substituting one for the other is the EVENT_CURRENT/CURRENT_MOMENT category error the repo forbids).

applicability_table.source_row: Sec 2.3.4 gate output clamped at 15.2 V; UCC27524 VDD 15 V
applicability_table.reason: Reference is a 15 V rail / 15.2 V internal clamp, not a measured gate-pin high level. Model case uses 12.6 V. Bias differs and the reference value is a design label, not a waveform.
The retained design guide does not publish device charge values; it names IPW60R099P6 and its voltage/current ratings only. Device-datasheet extraction (separate primary source) would be required.
Not published in the reference; and the model case multiplies Qgd by a hidden factor (0.5/1.0/1.5) that no reference can constrain.
Never published, and per the repo rule it must not be derived as Qg-Qgd or from total Qgs. The model case itself carries it as an explicit assumption (5e-9 / 1e-8 / 2e-8).
No Miller plateau voltage is published in the reference.

applicability_table.source_row: Sec 2.3.4 'This design uses a 22 ohm resistor'
applicability_table.source_conditions: series gate resistor, with antiparallel Schottky for turn-off
applicability_table.reason: Reference turn-on path is 22 ohm; model case uses a hypothetical 1.04/5.0/8.5 ohm driver-output-resistance assist on top of 10 ohm. The 22 ohm is real but different, and the model's driver profiles are hypothetical.
Device internal gate resistance not published in the reference.
A 5 A peak rating is not a dynamic source I-V curve or output impedance; the repo explicitly forbids inferring actual driver output impedance from the headline current.
Same as driver_source_peak_a.
No output-capacitance energy is published in the reference.
Commutation-loop inductance is not published. The model case carries it as an explicit 10 nH assumption.
The reference names the device but publishes no RDS(on); a temperature-resolved value would come from the device datasheet.
Numerical integration timestep chosen by the model, not a physical input a reference can supply.

applicability_table.source_row: Sec 2.3.4 22 ohm plus driver output path
applicability_table.reason: Turn-on external resistance is real (22 ohm) but the driver's series output path is unknown, so the applied value cannot be matched.

applicability_table.source_conditions: turn-off through an unspecified antiparallel diode
applicability_table.reason: The turn-off path is a diode, not a resistor. Its dynamic forward resistance at gate-drive currents is not published, so the turn-off external resistance cannot be resolved from the reference.
The reference never tests below 190 VAC; there is no 120 V operating point to compare with.
TI's measured Pin is for the whole board at 226-270 V line; the model case is 1796.31 W at 120 V. Not a matched comparison.
Whole-board input RMS only; not a per-switch quantity.

claim_testability.claim: Approximately 37 W switching-overlap loss on the boost switch at 120 V / 15 A / 400 V bus / 129.107 kHz (no-assist retained C7 case)
reasons: Operating point mismatch: no TI row at 120 V line, and the TI bus is a boost follower (400 V bus only near 270 V line).
Frequency mismatch: 45 kHz design / 44 kHz actual vs 129.107 kHz.
Device mismatch: IPW60R099P6 (600 V, 2 parallel) vs IPW65R045C7 (650 V, single-device model parameters).
Parallel-count mismatch: TI populates 2 MOSFETs (Q1, Q6) on a shared heatsink; the model's 37 W is a per-switch partial loss with no parallel sharing applied.
No switch event current, no per-switch RMS, no Eon/Eoff, no drain-current waveform, no per-device loss is published.
Qgd, current-transfer charge, plateau voltage, Eoss, loop inductance and RDS(on) are not published in the reference.

claim_testability.claim: A single-phase, non-interleaved CCM boost PFC with parallel MOSFETs using a 180 uH inductor can achieve >98% whole-board efficiency at 45 kHz and 230 V / up to 3.5 kW
reasons: Table 3-1 publishes measured whole-board Pin/Pout at 226-230 V, up to 3778.5 W in and 97.714-98.128% efficiency.
This is an architecture/whole-board plausibility reference only; it validates no switching-energy model term and must not be ranked against the model's partial per-switch loss.

claim_testability.claim: The whole-assembly loss of the model's 120 V / 400 V / 129 kHz design is below some measured bound
reasons: Whole-board Pin-Pout can bound a fully assembled model only at the same device, operating point and accounting boundary.

The model's published subtotal is a partial switch/gate loss (45.50 W no-assist) on a different device/point with an incomplete assembly ledger; comparing it against TI's 72.3-86.4 W whole-board loss is not a bound.

source_failures.failure: POUT (2560.7 W) > PIN (2513.6 W) while the printed efficiency is 97.974%; PIN*eff=2462.7 W. Internally inconsistent; excluded from all use.
POUT field printed 2.0102 W; VOUT*IOUT=2010.2 W and PIN*eff=2010.2 W. Decimal-field defect; excluded.
PIN field printed 2.1985 W; VIN*IIN*PF=2198.0 W, so POUT (2161.5 W) incorrectly exceeds the printed PIN. Decimal-field defect; excluded.
POUT field printed equal to PINAC (2687.4 W); VOUT*IOUT=2640.9 W and PIN*eff=2640.9 W. Excluded.
P=VI*PF identity not satisfied (276.0 vs 238.4; 722.8 vs 708.6; 2587.1 vs 2349.7 W). Table fields are mutually inconsistent at these rows; excluded.
Schematic and BOM are external downloads (TIDA-00779) and are not contained in the retained PDF. Parallel-MOSFET connection and per-device sharing cannot be confirmed from the retained bytes.

most_important_missing_source_row: A measured per-switch switching-transition capture on the boost MOSFET (or MOSFET pair) with simultaneous drain current and drain-source voltage on a stated time base, at a stated line phase and load, yielding the turn-on and turn-off event currents (and Eon/Eoff). TI publishes gate voltage, AC input voltage, Vds and AC input current only (Figures 3-6/3-7, printed p.13); it publishes no drain current, no event energy and no per-device loss.
